articles.dek: Iran's thousands of cheap one-way drones overwhelmed defenses built for a different kind of war, and Ukraine's drone arithmetic exposed how far behind the United States had fallen on scale, cost, and speed. items: estimated Shahed-family drones Iran launched between Feb. 28 and early April, with 2,210 aimed at the UAE alone.

The response:

articles.title: The U.S. closed the last big loophole in its AI chip ban — by going after the landlords
articles.dek: A rule that took effect today forces cloud operators to prove their compute isn't reaching China, and puts new license requirements on advanced GPUs headed to five countries.
articles.image_alt: Editorial illustration of a data center hall with glowing GPU server racks, a world map highlighting countries in Southeast Asia and South America, and a padlock over the racks
articles.caption: Illustration: Wire Willow. The rule follows the compute, not just the chips.

factbox.heading: The story in 30 seconds
items: The rule:
Published Nov 19 and effective immediately — an interim final rule from the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security.
Two controls:
A worldwide remote-access control keyed to 12 million aggregate TPP, and a license requirement for most advanced-GPU transfers to or within Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil.
Who's excepted:
U.S.-headquartered companies can use the five-country exception only by filing monthly reports with BIS.
What's not covered:
Infrastructure used only for commercial recommender systems is exempt; the rule also rescinds most of the Biden-era AI Diffusion Framework.

factbox.heading: The story in 30 seconds
items: The claim:
Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he worked with Claude for six weeks to build a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, written up in Lean and running to more than 250,000 pages.
The prize:
The Clay Mathematics Institute offers $1 million for the first correct solution of the 167-year-old problem, proposed by Bernhard Riemann in 1859.
The caveat:
The proof has not been verified, and checking it will take time. Oxford mathematician James Maynard says he is '98 or 99 percent certain' it is accurate — his assessment, not a confirmation.
The question:
It is unclear whether Claude was essential to the breakthrough, or a powerful tool in a mathematician's hands.

factbox.heading: The story in 30 seconds
items: The rethink:
Meta's 2026 sustainability report, published Nov 19, says the company is 're-evaluating' its 2030 net-zero goal and near-term targets.
The numbers:
Total emissions rose from 15.6 million to more than 21.7 million metric tonnes in a year — nearly 40% — and net emissions rose 45%, to more than 11.8 million tonnes.
The comparison:
Microsoft's footprint rose 25%, Google's 18% and Amazon's 16%; all three have stuck by their original goals so far.
The water:
Facility water use fell to 790 million gallons, but use in water-stressed areas rose to 246 million, and power-generation water use topped 26 billion gallons.

factbox.heading: The story in 30 seconds
items: The subpoena:

California Attorney General Rob Bonta served Nvidia an investigative subpoena on Thursday evening, November 19, asking whether its advanced chips or confidential information reached China and whether the company misled investors.
The halt:
Interim CEO Colette Kress told analysts Nvidia is “no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China,” and its forecast assumes no China data center compute revenue.
The caveat:
The subpoena opens an investigation, not a charge. No authority has accused Nvidia or Huang of sending chips to China; the criminal investigation is into Megaspeed, not Huang.
The stakes:
Licensed Hopper products brought in $2.4 billion from China in the quarter that ended October 25 — about 2 percent of Nvidia's $115.8 billion in quarterly revenue.

items: The order:
Report and Order FCC 26-81, adopted Thursday, November 19, 3–0, opens the 450 MHz band to drone command-and-control links and lets ground-based radar track drones in the 24.45 to 24.65 GHz band.
The license:
AURA Network Systems converts its 54 site-based licenses into one nationwide license, with a choice of two build-out tracks — high- or medium-altitude coverage, or low-altitude coverage at 400 feet.
The caveat:
The 800 MHz clarification is Commissioner Trusty's statement only; the final text's exact wording on drone use in that band is not confirmed by the sources read.
The timing:
Most rules take effect 30 days after Federal Register publication.

articles.title: Routine database maintenance took down three-quarters of ChatGPT
articles.dek: Between 1:48 and 5:21 p.m. PT on November 21, requests to ChatGPT and OpenAI's API failed at rates peaking at 75 percent — because the database replicas behind the login layer failed at the same time.
articles.image_alt: Editorial illustration of a server room with blinking red warning lights and a cracked database icon
articles.caption: Illustration: Wire Willow. Routine maintenance on one database service reached every product.

factbox.heading: The story in 30 seconds
items: The outage:
Requests to ChatGPT and OpenAI's API failed at rates peaking at 75 percent between 1:48 and 5:21 p.m. PT on Saturday, November 21 — 211 minutes, hitting paid and free users alike.
The cause:
Scheduled maintenance on a PostgresDB service used by OpenAI's Primary API service caused both read replicas to fail at the same time, cutting off authentication across the stack.
The fix:
Engineers brought two new replicas online in the same region; OpenAI has placed a moratorium on similar maintenance and shipped a feature flag to shift traffic off replicas.
The caveat:
All figures are OpenAI's own account of its own incident; no independent measure of the failure rate was available.

OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki proposes measuring AI progress by log-perplexity — a gauge of how well a model predicts the next token — and slowing development when it crosses agreed thresholds.

Sam Altman called the post the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while, and Elon Musk seemingly endorsed it.

briefs.title: Agile Robots closes a $500M Series F
briefs.body: Agile Robots closed a $500 million Series F led by SoftBank at an $8.5 billion valuation. Nvidia, Hitachi and T.Capital also took part, bringing the company’s total funding to about $2 billion.

briefs.title: Griffin raises $20M to add cards and stablecoin services
briefs.body: Griffin, a UK licensed bank for fintechs, raised $20 million in a Series B announced Nov. 12, led by Octagon Partners with Notion Capital, A+ Ventures, Nordic Ninja and Breega taking part, at a valuation above $100 million. The plan is to expand into card issuing — branded retail and corporate debit cards, with credit to follow — and stablecoin services, including reserve services for stablecoin businesses and on-chain cross-border payments. Those are planned services, not launched, and no rollout schedule was given.

briefs.title: Anthropic opens a private beta for self-hosted Claude Managed Agents
briefs.body: Anthropic opened a private beta on Nov. 12 that lets companies run the Claude Managed Agents service — the harness, sandboxes, credentials and session history — in their own cloud or on-premises. The model itself does not move: model requests still go to Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google’s Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or the customer’s own gateway. Access is by request through an Anthropic account team, with no pricing or general-availability date given. This is a private beta only — not a general release and not a fully offline Claude. The same day, Anthropic launched Claude for Manufacturing for Team and Enterprise plans, with 17 skills and connectors for Autodesk Fusion, Infor, Microsoft 365 and Oracle NetSuite.

briefs.title: UFORCE raises $700M to build Ukraine's drone arsenal at scale
briefs.body: UFORCE, the London-headquartered, Ukrainian-founded maker of uncrewed sea, air, and land systems, raised a $700 million Series A at a $6 billion valuation on November 12, co-led by Valor Equity Partners and the UK National Wealth Fund, which put in £113 million (about $150 million) — the fund's largest defense investment to date — with the U.S.–Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund also taking part. The company says its MAGURA sea drones contributed to the destruction of more than a dozen Russian warships, and its NEMESIS strike drones have flown more than 300,000 combat flights; those figures are the company's own and have not been independently verified. No revenue was disclosed.

briefs.title: Microsoft's Ignite brings specialist AI models for coding, security, and small decisions
briefs.body: At Ignite, Microsoft announced MAI Code 2 for agentic coding, MAI Cyber 2 Flash with 12 billion active parameters for cybersecurity, and Microsoft-Decision-1.1 for routing, classification, and verification tasks too small for a large general model. It also introduced Agent 365 Business Analytics to tie AI spending to business outcomes. Separately, Microsoft said on November 13 it will switch the small language model built into Windows from Phi Silica to the 2.3-billion-parameter Aion Instruct.

briefs.title: After a week of outages, a bipartisan bill would create a board to investigate AI and cyber failures
briefs.body: Reps. Morgan Luttrell (R-Texas) and Ritchie Torres (D-N.Y.) introduced the ROOT CAUSE Act on Wednesday to establish a National Cyber and AI Investigations Board inside CISA, to determine why significant incidents happened and recommend ways to prevent them from recurring. The bill follows a nationwide FAA ground stop that delayed more than 10,000 flights, a Microsoft outage that disrupted workplace tools, and an outage on the NSA's classified NSANet network. A companion proposal, the AI INSIGHT Act from Rep. Matt Van Epps, would direct CISA to help agencies identify AI agents on federal networks and limit their access.

briefs.title: WIRED: the Nvidia board's problem with Huang was his 'lack of candor'
briefs.body: WIRED reports, citing sources, that the Nvidia board's main issue ahead of Jensen Huang's resignation was the former chief executive's 'lack of candor' — amid allegations of multiple affairs, including with a direct report and an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. The board said on November 17 it 'does not intend' to reinstate Huang as CEO.

briefs.title: An AI debt-collection service exposed 6.6 million accounts and 315,000 call recordings
briefs.body: Two serious vulnerabilities in CreditNirvana, an AI debt-collection platform, would have let attackers access 6.6 million accounts and 315,000 call recordings — along with emails, texts and credit reports. The bugs were patched in June and disclosed in October.

briefs.title: After a week of talks, the UN agrees to two more years of talking about 'killer robots'
briefs.body: After a week of negotiations in Geneva that ran until 4:30 a.m. on Saturday, 128 countries agreed to spend two years 'elaborating' on a possible accord on lethal autonomous weapons — not 'negotiating' one, a word several countries rejected. About 100 countries had pushed for swift, legally binding rules; the United States, Russia and Israel opposed them. The International Committee of the Red Cross, which wanted binding rules within a year, said it regretted the outcome, and the Stop Killer Robots coalition called the mandate 'watered down.'

briefs.title: Anthropic's first day as a public company: up 34 percent
briefs.body: Anthropic's shares opened on the Nasdaq on Thursday at $111.50, about 34 percent above the $83 IPO price set on Wednesday — the market's first verdict on the biggest initial public offering in history. The offering closed on Friday with the underwriters exercising their full option for 147 million additional shares, bringing gross proceeds to about $93.5 billion, with about $91.6 billion going to the company. The separate $26 billion private placement to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC also closed.

briefs.title: Payhawk's $280M, Dave's bank charter, and the World Bank's stablecoin test
briefs.body: Payhawk raised a $280 million Series C at a $2 billion valuation, led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives — the day's biggest fintech round. Dave, the mobile banking app, filed with the OCC and the FDIC for a national bank charter to form Dave Bank, N.A., and crypto payments company MoonPay filed for a charter of its own, for a stablecoin-issuing arm. And the World Bank Group said it will test USDC disbursements with Citi and Circle, while DBS opened direct USDC minting and redemption to institutional clients through a Circle partnership.

briefs.title: 151 humanoid robots danced in Shenzhen — and set a world record
briefs.body: One hundred and fifty-one humanoid robots performed a synchronized dance routine in Shenzhen on November 17, setting a Guinness World Record for the most humanoid robots dancing simultaneously within one hour. The event beat its initial target of 110 robots, and adjudicator Xiong Wen confirmed all 151 machines completed the performance. Twenty of ENGINEAI's full-size T800 humanoids — 1.73 meters tall, about 75 kilograms — demonstrated the company's swarm-control capabilities, joined by groups of Unitree G1 and AGIBOT X2 robots. The Shenzhen Longgang District Artificial Intelligence (Robotics) Bureau organized the event ahead of the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting on November 18–19. It was a choreographed showcase, not a capability test — but coordinating 151 bipedal machines to move in step is itself the hard part of the humanoid problem.

briefs.title: Anthropic's day two: down 8.5 percent, and $109 billion gone
briefs.body: Anthropic's record IPO met reality on its second day of trading. Shares closed Friday, November 20, at $88.91, down 8.5 percent, after trading as low as $83.05 — five cents above the $83 IPO price — shedding about $109 billion in market value in a day, according to The Wall Street Journal. The slide came as the Nasdaq fell about 5.3 percent on Friday in a broad AI sell-off the Journal says sealed a $4 trillion wipeout of market value in the Nasdaq that week. Retail buyers who chased Thursday's open at $111.50 were sitting on losses of roughly 20 percent by Friday's close, and the Journal reports the offering allocated less than 20 percent of shares to retail investors. Anthropic closed its first session Thursday at $97.17, up 17 percent. The IPO itself closed Friday with the underwriters exercising their full option for 147 million additional shares, bringing gross proceeds to about $93.5 billion. On December 15, another roughly 300 million shares become available to trade, which could pressure the stock further.

briefs.title: Google puts Genie 4 on the Gemini API — a world you can walk through, at about 10 cents a second
briefs.body: Google made its interactive world model Genie 4 available to developers through the Gemini API and Google AI Studio on November 19, a day after it opened in Project Genie for eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers. Starting from a text prompt, a reference image, or both, developers can generate continuous 720p worlds at 24 frames per second with synchronized native audio — ambient soundscapes, sound effects, and character dialogue — and steer them with keyboard controls and new text prompts as they unfold. Every output carries an imperceptible SynthID watermark. Sessions are capped at 120 seconds, and Google's own documentation warns that object permanence is strongest in roughly the first 45 to 90 seconds — turn away and a building may have moved when you turn back. Access is paid only: a third-party breakdown of Google's pricing page puts the cost at roughly $0.10 per second, about $6.05 a minute.

briefs.title: Amazon's Atlanta drone deliveries started without a public filing
briefs.body: Amazon's Prime Air began drone deliveries from Gwinnett County, metro Atlanta, the weekend of November 14–15, using its MK30 drone to deliver items under 5 pounds within 7.5 miles in under an hour, for fees of $2.99 to $4.99, creating about 30 local jobs. But unlike Wing, the Alphabet-owned drone delivery company that also serves the Atlanta area, Amazon's launch left no public environmental review document on the FAA's drone index for Georgia. Wing went through a site-specific environmental assessment with a public comment period that drew zero comments during its July-to-August review window. Amazon, by contrast, relied on a national environmental finding the FAA signed in 2025 covering its Part 135 drone delivery operations broadly — a blanket approval that lets individual city launches proceed through internal FAA review without triggering a new public notice. Amazon has issued no official newsroom post announcing the Atlanta launch; it was first reported by local Atlanta outlets.
